Pricing

XERJ is free. Apache-2.0, no tiers.

There is nothing to buy. The xerj binary, the MCP server inside it, and the corpus packs xerj ask downloads are all free, with no account, no sign-up and no API key. The source is on GitHub under the Apache License 2.0, so you can run it, change it and ship it inside your own product. The only costs are the machine it runs on and the tokens your agent spends.

Install · Linux and macOS curl -fsSL https://xerj.org/get | sh

What is free

Everything in the binary

The engineFull-text (BM25), kNN, hybrid, aggregations, the Elasticsearch-compatible REST API on :9200 and the native API on :8080, agent memory, the link index. One build; no feature is held back.
xerj ask and the Corpus HubThe signed catalogue and its pre-indexed packs are public GitHub Release assets. Browsing hub.xerj.org needs no account.
MCP serverxerj mcp, 17 tools, in the same binary. xerj init wires it into Claude Code and Cursor.
Air-gapped installsThe air-gapped recipe is for everyone: stage the release and an optional neural model on a connected machine, then run with no internet access.
LicenceApache License 2.0. Code contributions need the CLA; field-report pull requests are exempt.

What it costs you

Your machine and your agent's tokens

  • Hardware. The install guide lists about 400 MB of RAM idle and a 2 GB working set per active index. Large ingests grow the server's memory with document count; the sizing note in llms.txt has one observed data point.
  • Disk for packs. xerj ask keeps pulled packs under a 4 GB budget and evicts the least recently used first. The lz4 pack is 4.4 MB; zstd is 20.1 MB.
  • Tokens. The search itself runs no model. Your agent still pays for what it reads; in the reference-coding study the XERJ arm cost $1.58 against $3.27 for the grep-driven arm and $11.18 from memory alone (16 runs per arm, 8 tasks).
  • Neural embeddings, if you want them. The default embedder is lexical and needs nothing. --embed-mode neural downloads a model of about 90 MB once.

What is not offered

No SLA, no cluster, no sales team

  • No paid edition or support contract. The project does not document one anywhere. Earlier versions of this page listed Professional and Enterprise tiers with support terms; those described plans, not a product.
  • No high availability. XERJ runs as a single node with no replication or failover. If you need a replicated cluster, use Elasticsearch or OpenSearch for that workload.
  • Help is public. Bugs and questions go to GitHub issues or a Discussion, and there is a Discord. Response is best-effort.

Pay it back with one field report

The project asks one thing for the binary: after you use it, a short report of what you pointed it at and your honest verdict. xerj feedback --submit opens the pull request, or an agent calls the xerj_field_report MCP tool. Ask your first question or read the docs.
